placements.why: The content describes a structural contract for how the remember operation works asynchronously — receipt, cursor polling, piggybacked reactions — which is an architectural decision about system design, not a fact or measurement. No existing strata or narrative leaf exists to hold it.
placements.title: From blocking calls to async job contracts
placements.theme: System operations that once blocked now return immediate receipts and defer completion to polled or piggybacked channels.

placements.title: Remember becomes a dispatch-and-poll job, not a blocking call
placements.theme: The remember operation returns an immediate receipt and defers extraction to a polled cursor, with reactions piggybacked on later calls, so no client drop loses work.
placements.why: Both segments cohere under one thematic read of the async remember contract: src-1 ratifies the receipt-and-cursor-polling shape with no blocking call and no lost work on a dropped receipt, while src-2 asserts the dispatch-then-poll-or-piggyback decision. This is a directional statement about how the system's core operation is structured — a subject future envelopes will keep feeding — not a one-time fact.
